name: Telecommunications
title: Network incident evidence coordination
summary: Correlate alarms, service dependencies, and change history before an operator approves network remediation.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A telecom operations center receives thousands of alarms after a regional service degradation. Teams must identify shared dependencies, determine affected services, and inspect recent changes. The illustrative system assembles incident evidence and proposes runbook steps while network operators retain production control.
problem: Alarm volume can hide the initiating fault, topology may be stale, and a recent change can be coincidental. A model-driven rollback without current dependency checks could widen an outage or interrupt unaffected customers.
whyAgents: Alarm triage, topology analysis, change investigation, and runbook specialists work in parallel. Deterministic correlation rules and topology queries produce the affected-service set; the orchestrator limits hypothesis loops and preserves operator ownership.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Track preparation time and diagnostic quality alongside service restoration outcomes. The architecture should make uncertainty and action boundaries visible during pressure, rather than reward fluent incident narratives that outpace the evidence.

agents.name: Alarm correlation agent
agents.responsibility: Group repeated alarms by resource, time window, and known dependency.
agents.boundary: Cannot suppress critical alarms or redefine severity.

agents.name: Service impact agent
agents.responsibility: Trace affected resources to customer services and redundancy paths.
agents.boundary: Cannot assume a stale topology edge remains operational.

agents.name: Change investigator
agents.responsibility: Compare approved changes and configuration snapshots with incident timing.
agents.boundary: Cannot roll back or edit network configuration.

agents.name: Runbook coordinator
agents.responsibility: Retrieve approved diagnostic steps and draft an operator execution plan.
agents.boundary: Only allowlisted read diagnostics can run without separate production-change approval.

systems.name: Operations support systems
systems.role: Supply alarms, resource inventory, service models, and authoritative incident identifiers.

systems.name: Change and configuration platforms
systems.role: Retain approved changes, device snapshots, and operator execution records.

systems.name: Controlled automation gateway
systems.role: Executes scoped diagnostics or approved changes with preconditions, rate limits, and receipts.

flow.title: Open incident context
flow.description: Deduplicate alarm bursts, assign an incident commander, and establish observation windows and diagnostic budgets.

flow.title: Correlate symptoms
flow.description: Group alarms using configured rules and retain representative raw events so compression cannot hide distinct failures.

flow.title: Trace impact
flow.description: Query service dependencies with inventory freshness metadata and separate confirmed affected services from possible exposure.

flow.title: Inspect changes
flow.description: Compare incident timing with approved changes and configuration differences; label causal hypotheses as provisional.

flow.title: Stage diagnostic plan
flow.description: Present safe diagnostic steps, expected observations, rollback prerequisites, and uncertainty for operator selection.

flow.title: Execute bounded action
flow.description: The gateway rechecks device state and approval scope, performs the authorized step, and evaluates service evidence before further action.

diagrams.title: Failure and decision sequence
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant O as "Case orchestrator"
    participant S as "Operations support systems"
    participant H as "Accountable reviewer"
O->>S: Read alarms and service topology
    S-->>O: Candidate protection path
    O->>S: Validate live path health
    S-->>O: Protection unavailable
    O->>H: Block disruptive plan and show evidence
    H-->>O: Select safe diagnostic path
diagrams.caption: Topology shows a protection path that has already failed. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: Topology shows a protection path that has already failed.
failures.detection: Current device health disagrees with the stored dependency graph.
failures.recovery: Mark redundancy unknown and block plans that rely on the unavailable protection path.

failures.scenario: Repeated remediation creates an oscillating configuration.
failures.detection: Action history detects alternating states or an exceeded iteration budget.
failures.recovery: Stop automation, preserve traces, and return control to the incident commander.

controls: Never expose unrestricted device shells or configuration credentials to model prompts.
Bound diagnostics by device set, command allowlist, timeout, and incident budget.
Require operator approval for service-affecting changes and rollback execution.
Check topology freshness and live protection state before recommending disruption.
Preserve raw alarms and action receipts behind every compressed incident narrative.

metrics.name: Incident briefing latency
metrics.definition: Time from incident declaration to a source-backed impact and hypothesis packet.

metrics.name: Impact precision
metrics.definition: Services confirmed affected divided by services flagged as affected in audited incidents.

metrics.name: Diagnostic usefulness
metrics.definition: Approved diagnostics producing a discriminating observation divided by diagnostics executed.

metrics.name: Automation containment
metrics.definition: Attempts blocked for exceeded device, command, or iteration scope divided by attempted actions.

tradeoffs.cost: Can conceal independent faults unless raw evidence remains inspectable.
Accuracy depends on inventory and live-state freshness.
Operator availability becomes part of restoration latency.

rollout.acceptance: Operators validate alarm grouping, service impact, and unsupported-causality detection across incident classes.
One region permits bounded diagnostics after command allowlist and data-access tests pass.
A small runbook set launches after oscillation, stale-topology, and rollback-precondition exercises succeed.
